title: Idempotency key is minted per click, so a retry after an unconfirmed refund is a new request and can refund twice
evidence: app.js:114-117 builds a fresh key on every call; app.js:128 passes it inline and never stores it. On failure (app.js:131-133) state.selected is left intact and no reload runs, so the same ids stay selected and the button is re-enabled in the finally block (app.js:135-136). api.js:32 and README.md:9 present the key as the guard against a repeated refund.
failing_case: Select 2 orders, click Refund, confirm. The server processes the refund but the connection drops (or a gateway returns 504). request() throws, the UI says 'The refund was not confirmed'. The selection is still checked and the button is live. The user clicks Refund again and confirms; a new UUID is sent, so the server's idempotency check does not match and the same orders are refunded a second time (unless the server independently rejects already-refunded orders, which nothing in this repo shows).
remediation: Create the key once per attempt and keep it with the picked ids (for example in state) until the server answers definitively; reuse it on retry for the same id set, and discard it only on a confirmed success or a confirmed 4xx rejection. Also reload the orders after a failed refund so the user sees real statuses.

title: normaliseOrder turns a missing total (null, "", [], true) into a valid order worth $0.00 or $1.00
evidence: Number(null) is 0, Number("") is 0, Number([]) is 0, Number(true) is 1, and all pass Number.isFinite on domain.js:12. The comment at domain.js:7 and the 'incomplete data' message at app.js:103 say such records are dropped. Negative totals also pass (domain.js:12). Traced from JS coercion rules; node was not approved to run the probe.
failing_case: The API returns {"id": 7, "total": null, "status": "paid"}. The row renders as $0.00, counts in 'Orders' and drags down 'Average per order', and no 'could not be shown' note appears. A negative total such as -50 on a paid order reduces Revenue. The user can also select the $0.00 row and send it to the refund endpoint.
remediation: Accept only typeof raw.total === 'number' or a non-empty numeric string, reject values below 0 (or make refunds/credits an explicit case), and add a unit test for null, empty string, array, boolean and negative inputs.

quote: const amount = picked.reduce((sum, o) => sum + o.total, 0);
title: The refund amount shown in the confirmation is computed in the click handler with float addition and ignores the domain's pricing rules
evidence: domain.js:25-30 defines what an order is worth (gold discount, then sales tax, in whole cents). app.js:122 instead adds raw dollar floats inline, so the amount the user approves is a second, different rule for the same money and is not unit-tested. Rubric 1, Domain leaks: arithmetic on money inside a UI file.
failing_case: Select a paid gold order with total 100.00. Revenue stat treats it as 100*0.9*1.0825 = $97.43 (domain.js:28-29); the confirmation dialog says 'totalling $100.00'. The two figures for the same order disagree and nothing says which is what the customer gets back. Summing many dollar floats also drifts from the cent-exact approach that domain.js:2 sets out.
remediation: Add a pure refundAmountCents(orders) in domain.js, use integer cents, decide with the owner what a refund of a discounted/taxed order is, test it, and have app.js only format the result. Better, have the server return the amount to confirm.

title: Success toast is shown for the whole batch without reading the refund response
evidence: api.js:34-38 returns the parsed body, and app.js:128 discards it. Only res.ok is checked (api.js:15). README.md:13 claims success is reported 'only after the server confirms it'. A batch endpoint taking an array of ids can answer 200/207 with per-id outcomes; none is read. The same code treats a 200/204 with an empty body as a failure (api.js:16-20, then app.js:133), so a refund that did succeed shows as 'not confirmed'.
failing_case: POST /refunds with 5 ids; the server refunds 3 and answers 200 {"refunded":[...3], "failed":[...2]}. The toast says 'Refunded 5 orders.' and the reload then clears the selection, so the user has no cue which 2 failed. Inferred: the response shape is not in the repo.
remediation: Define the response contract, check per-id results, and report 'Refunded 3 of 5; 2 failed: ids ...' and keep the failed ids selected. Treat an empty 2xx body as success for this call.

quote: With 10,000 orders from a mocked local API, a search re-renders in under 100 ms; this has not been measured against the real API.
title: README states measurements and an axe-core result that have no script or artifact in the repo
evidence: The repo holds six files: no mock API, benchmark, axe config or test. README.md:5 'axe-core reports no WCAG 2.1 A or AA violations' and README.md:11 cannot be reproduced. README.md:12 gives a Team plan price that nothing in an order dashboard uses.
failing_case: A reader who wants to confirm the 100 ms or the axe result has nothing to run; the 'Pricing' paragraph also describes a product that is not in this code.
remediation: Commit the mock-API and axe scripts that produced the numbers, or label the claims as unmeasured; remove the unrelated Pricing bullet.

title: Paging with the keyboard disables the focused button and does not announce the new page
evidence: Pressing Enter on Previous/Next at the second or second-to-last page re-renders with that same button disabled (app.js:71-72); focus sits on a disabled control. #page (index.html:34) is a plain span with no live region, so a screen-reader user hears nothing when the page changes. README.md:5 says every control is reachable and status is announced elsewhere but not-tested with a screen reader. Traced, not driven.
failing_case: Keyboard user on page 2 of 3 presses Enter on Next: page 3 renders, Next becomes disabled while focused, the key no longer works and focus order is lost; a screen reader announces nothing about 'Page 3 of 3'.
remediation: Make #page a role=status/aria-live=polite element, and when a pager button becomes disabled move focus to the other pager button (or use aria-disabled instead of disabled).
